The decision was taken on Tuesday at a Special General Meeting in Kaduna by the Secretaries to the Governments of the 19 states, who represented their respective governments as shareholders.
The dissolution will take effect upon the adoption of the relevant ordinary resolutions at a duly convened General Meeting and compliance with applicable statutory requirements.
Addressing journalists after the meeting, the Secretary to the Gombe State Government, Prof. Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, said the shareholders had resolved to undertake a comprehensive reorganisation of the company.
He said the exercise was aimed at strengthening NNDC’s institutional capacity, improving corporate governance, enhancing operational efficiency and repositioning it to serve the collective economic interests of the 19 Northern states.
Njodi said a new Board of Directors would be constituted to provide strategic leadership, policy direction, effective supervision and corporate oversight.
He explained that the composition, nomination and appointment of the new directors would reflect the ownership interests of the participating states, the company’s Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the provisions of the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020. According to him, the shareholders would subsequently approve the nominations and appointments in line with the company’s constitutional documents and applicable laws.
The incoming board has also been mandated to review the existing management structure, personnel, administrative arrangements, operational framework and overall performance of the company.
Njodi said the board would take appropriate measures to strengthen management, improve accountability and professionalism, and enhance corporate performance in accordance with its statutory and fiduciary responsibilities.
He disclosed that the new board would also conduct a comprehensive corporate governance, financial, administrative and operational audit of the company.
The audit will examine NNDC’s financial position, assets and liabilities, existing investments, subsidiaries, joint ventures and other commercial interests.
It will also assess the performance and profitability of the company’s investments, compliance with statutory and regulatory obligations, corporate governance standards, contractual commitments and outstanding liabilities.
Njodi said the audit would further evaluate the effectiveness of the previous board and management structure, alongside other issues considered necessary to protect and advance the interests of the shareholders.
He added that the findings and recommendations would be presented to the shareholders at a subsequent General Meeting.
The outgoing board and management have been directed to facilitate an orderly handover of the company’s affairs, including records, account books, statutory documents, financial records, assets, properties, contracts and other institutional materials, upon the lawful assumption of office by their successors.
Njodi stressed that the incoming board must ensure that all company assets and interests were adequately protected during the transition, warning against any unauthorised disposal, transfer, encumbrance or alienation of the company’s assets.
He said the shareholders had reviewed the company’s corporate governance structure, operational performance, management arrangements and the effectiveness of the existing board before reaching the decision.
According to him, the restructuring was considered necessary in the overriding interests of the company, its shareholders and the economic development aspirations of Northern Nigeria.
Njodi said the shareholders were exercising their statutory powers under Section 288 of CAMA 2020, which provides for the removal of directors by ordinary resolution, subject to compliance with the applicable statutory procedures and the company’s Articles of Association.
He added that the shareholders were committed to restoring confidence, accountability, transparency, professionalism and effective corporate governance in the administration of NNDC.
